old.name: Kastella / Profitis Ilias
old.teaser: The postcard hill — Ziller villas stacked in an amphitheatre above the sea.
old.text: Munichia rises about 86 m over the port, its neoclassical and interwar villas falling in tiers to the water; Piraeans call the sea-facing slope Kastella, the landward side Profitis Ilias. Ernst Ziller bought land at Plateia Alexandras in 1875 and raised the row still called Ziller's neighbourhood. The crown carries the open-air Veakeio and the Profitis Ilias church terrace, the whole Saronic at your feet. Now the most gentrified address in the port — come for the climb and the light, not a scene.
old.meta: BEST · golden hour and sunset from the hill; summer evenings for the Veakeio

old.name: Mikrolimano / Munichia
old.teaser: The smallest ancient harbour — a crescent of masts, fish tables and touts.
old.text: The smallest and most theatrical of the three ancient harbours — the war port of Munichia, Tourkolimano until 1967 — now a crescent of masts, sailing-club dinghies and waterside tables. Asia Minor refugees filled its shore with shacks after 1922; the first grand psarotavernes appeared around 1960. Serious, award-listed kitchens sit cheek by jowl with view-trading traps: choose by name, never by the tout at the door. Arguably the most photographed corner of Piraeus.
old.meta: BEST · evening over the water, or early morning for the boats; skip high-summer weekend lunch

old.name: Pasalimani / Zea
old.teaser: The round middle harbour where the city actually lives — cafés round the water.
old.text: The middle harbour: a near-circular basin, antiquity's largest of Athens's three war ports, named Zea for its superior grain, its stone shipsheds once holding the bulk of the trireme fleet; the Ottomans left the name Pasalimani. Today it is Marina Zeas, the everyday promenade where the city lives — cafés and cocktail bars ringing the water, the Hellenic Maritime Museum on its shoulder, yachts swinging on their lines. Polished and busy, not a postcard.
old.meta: BEST · evening for the volta and drinks; weekends for its liveliest café life

old.name: Piraiki / Akti Themistokleous
old.teaser: The sunset quarter — flat swimming rocks and the ancient Long Walls at the tideline.
old.text: The south-western edge, the most romantic stretch of the peninsula: a long west-facing shore of flat swimming rocks, tiny coves and low houses running to the tip, with the ruined Long Walls of Conon surfacing along the waterline. Locals swim off the rocks all summer; at Aphrodite cove the island-style chapel of Agios Nikolaos and a standing cross mark where the Saronic turns molten at sundown. The €23.5m Piraiki Riviera promenade, tendered 2025, will smarten it; for now, gloriously unglamorous next to Kastella.
old.meta: BEST · sunset above all (west-facing); summer daytime for swimming off the rocks

old.name: Freattyda
old.teaser: A pocket beach inside a working port, on an ancient court for the accused.
old.text: A compact quarter on the south-eastern lip, just below Zea, carrying a surprising weight of antiquity: this was the Phreattys, the open-air court where Athenians accused of involuntary homicide pleaded from a boat while the jury sat on shore. Its cove was reshaped in the 1960s and now cradles a small organised beach — a pocket summer paradise inside a working port. The quiet hinge where the marina promenade turns into the wilder Piraiki coast.
old.meta: BEST · summer for the beach; late afternoon into sunset as the coast opens west

old.name: Terpsithea
old.teaser: Central, genuinely local — four squares where you watch the city be a city.
old.text: One of the most central and genuinely local quarters, named for the big square where the two spinal avenues cross — Iroon Polytechneiou climbing to Hatzikyriakeio, 2as Merarchias running from the central port down to Zea. The roughly 20-stremmata plateia splits into four smaller squares, each with its own feel; the blocks around are everyday residential Piraeus — kafeneia, bakeries, ordinary tavernes serving the neighbourhood, not the tourist. None of Kastella's drama, and that is exactly the value.
old.meta: BEST · weekday daytime and early evening, for café life and the local squares

quartiers:Kentro & the Central Port / Ti.group: The working port & the refugee city

old.group: The working port & the refugee city
old.name: Kentro & the Central Port / Tinaneios
old.teaser: The working heart — ferry gates, the 1869 railway, and a shaded 1854 garden.
old.text: The working heart most travellers only pass through: the Kantharos commercial harbour, the Aegean ferry gates and Greece's oldest railway terminus — the Athens–Piraeus line of 1869 — all converge on Plateia Karaiskaki. The marble Lion that gave the port its medieval name Porto Leone was hauled to Venice in 1687; a block inland the Tinaneios Garden, laid out under Admiral de Tinan in 1854, gives a rare shaded pause. Come as arrival ritual and provisioning nerve, not a stroll.
old.meta: BEST · early morning for a quiet coffee before the crowds; the Tinaneios garden any weekday afternoon

quartiers:Nikaia / Kokkinia.group: The working port & the refugee city

old.group: The working port & the refugee city
old.name: Nikaia / Kokkinia
old.teaser: The great 1922 refugee quarter — streets named for the lost cities of Asia Minor.
old.text: The great refugee quarter, and the antidote to Kastella's polish. When 1.5 million Greeks were uprooted from Asia Minor in 1922, Nea Kokkinia was founded here in 1923 — 33,000 people by the 1928 census, the most populous refugee colony of all — its grid named street by street for lost eastern cities: Smyrnis, Aidiniou, Attaleias, Kaisareias. The Battle and Blockade of August 1944, 'Bloody Kokkinia', is still commemorated; the church of Osia Xeni anchors the centre. A living archive of Mikrasiatika flavours, largely untouched by tourism.
old.meta: BEST · weekday daytime for the street market, the Asia-Minor grid and a history walk

quartiers:Drapetsona.group: The working port & the refugee city

old.group: The working port & the refugee city
old.name: Drapetsona
old.teaser: The refugee-industrial quarter of a famous lament, its poisoned shore reborn.
old.text: West of the central port, the other great refugee-and-industrial quarter — after 1922 the largest shanty settlement in Attica, 36,485 people by 1928, its life bound to the shipyards and above all the Lipasmata fertiliser works. That smoke and hardship gave Greece one of its defining laments, 'Drapetsona' (Theodorakis and Livaditis, made famous by Bithikotsis around 1960). The Lipasmata closed in 1999 and its poisoned shoreline reopened as a coastal park. Still working-class and meraklidiko, with some of the most honest eating in the port.
old.meta: BEST · late afternoon into sunset at the Lipasmata park; evenings for the harbourside fish tavernes

old.name: The Kastella–Mikrolimano loop
old.teaser: Fishing harbour below, an amphitheatre of houses above
old.text: Mikrolimano was ancient Munichia, smallest of the three war-harbours, sacred to Artemis; eighty-plus neosoikoi once ringed the basin where the fish restaurants now sit. Above it Kastella rises in tiers, and the ancient theatre of Munichia faced the hill where the modern Veakeio stands. This is the Piraeus Melina Mercouri and Jules Dassin filmed in 1960 for 'Never on Sunday'. A twenty-minute climb lays the whole Saronic flat below you. Not for anyone avoiding steep steps — the harbour's fish tavernas run among the priciest in Piraeus.
old.meta: START Mikrolimano esplanade · ~2–3 km with stairs, 1–2 hr · free

old.name: The Zea (Pasalimani) marina round
old.teaser: A flat circuit of a perfectly round ancient war-harbour
old.text: Zea was the largest of the three ancient harbours, its shore lined with about 196 neosoikoi that housed Athens' trireme fleet; the remains still lie under the modern marina. The Hellenic Maritime Museum, at Zea since 1971, keeps a length of the 4th-century Konon wall in situ, so the loop reads two and a half millennia of the same basin in one round. The yachts swing where the triremes once dried. Not for a swim — a working marina ringed by café-bars, prices cosmopolitan.
old.meta: START Marina Zeas, by the Maritime Museum · ~1.5 km flat circuit · free

old.name: Up Profitis Ilias to the Veakeio
old.teaser: The city's balcony — an open-air theatre over the gulf
old.text: Profitis Ilias is the ancient Munichia, its little theatre once facing the classical stage below in Mikrolimano. The modern amphitheatre was poured in 1969 as the 'Skylitseio', renamed in 1976 the Veakeio for the Piraeus actor Emilios Veakis; 2,000 seats climb the slope, and from the 87-metre summit the sea, port and islands lie open at once. On summer nights you watch ancient drama under the stars. Outside June to September the theatre is dark, and little else holds the summit at midday.
old.meta: START Profitis Ilias summit, above Mikrolimano · hill free, theatre ticketed · Veakeio Jun–Sep evenings

walks:The Piraiki coast walk to the ligh.group: The coast and the ancient trace

old.name: The Piraiki coast walk to the lighthouse
old.teaser: A sea-wall shore ending at the ancient lighthouse
old.text: The road traces the ancient Themistoclean sea-wall, and in places the surf still breaks over cut blocks of Conon's 4th-century-BC wall. Midway the shore opens at Aphrodite cove, Baikoutsi, under the tall concrete Cross of the Unknown Sailor and the island-style chapel of Agios Nikolaos; near the tip stands the ancient lighthouse, once mistaken for the tomb of Themistocles. Go 90 minutes before dusk — the shore faces due west. No sand, no shade, hard swimming ledges.
old.meta: START Freattyda / Akti Themistokleous · ~2.5 km, ~1.5 hr one way · free

walks:The Hippodamian grid & the Eetione.group: The coast and the ancient trace

old.name: The Hippodamian grid & the Eetioneia Gate walls
old.teaser: The largest walkable stretch of the port's 5th-century-BC walls
old.text: Around the mid-5th century BC Hippodamus of Miletus laid Piraeus out on a rational grid, and Themistocles' walls, completed 471 BC, wrapped it in stone. The Eetioneia Gate, built 411 BC on the Kastraki knoll, was one of only two land gates; long buried, it was excavated, opened to the public in 2018 and floodlit by 2024. You now walk the largest surviving stretch of the fortification, staring down at the moored ferries. Not a café stroll — an exposed archaeological site inside a working port, with limited opening days.
old.meta: HOURS summer (1 Apr–31 Oct) 08:30–15:30, closed Wed; winter Tue/Sat/Sun · free/low · Eetioneia knoll, western arm

walks:The central-port arcades & the Mun.group: The coast and the ancient trace

old.name: The central-port arcades & the Municipal Theatre
old.teaser: Belle-époque grid meets the working port, on ancient street-lines
old.text: Piraeus is the cradle of port rebetiko: after 1922 the refugees crammed the harbour quarters, and here Markos Vamvakaris and the Piraeus school forged bouzouki-driven rebetiko in the tekedes — a music UNESCO inscribed as world heritage in 2017. Against that working-class grain rises Ioannis Lazarimos' Municipal Theatre of 1895, Corinthian-porticoed. Down at the water the medieval name Porto Leone still recalls the marble Lion the Venetians hauled off in 1687. Not a pedestrianised old town — a gritty, working port centre with traffic between the gems.
old.meta: START Municipal Theatre, Korai Square · ~3 km, ~40–60 min · free

calas:Votsalakia Municipal Beach.group: In town: the pebble and the rock

old.name: Votsalakia Municipal Beach
old.teaser: The rebuilt town beach, and the winter-swimmers' spot
old.text: The most-swum patch of Piraeus water, rebuilt in 2025 for €2M with five sports courts, LED lighting and a Seatrac ramp with an amphibious wheelchair. On 6 September 2025 swimmers revived the open-water course of the 1896 Olympics, pushing off here and stroking about 1,200 m to Pier K of Zea, 129 years on. All winter it belongs to the year-round plungers. Swim after dry spells, not after rain.
old.meta: FREE · lifeguard late May–Oct · wheelchair sea-access · water state-rated suitable, PAKOE flags sections

calas:Freattyda Municipal Beach.group: In town: the pebble and the rock

old.name: Freattyda Municipal Beach
old.teaser: A monitored city strip beside a WWII submarine's turret
old.text: The one Piraeus swim the state actually monitors, a designated EU bathing water since 1990, rated suitable, though the same profile scores the water only 'Moderate' and names Zea marina a pollution source. When the marina was dug out in the early 1960s the old cove was abolished and this artificial ~400 m strip built in its place. In the yard of the Naval Museum beside it stands the conning tower of the Papanikolis, the most decorated Greek submarine of the war. Best glassy at dawn.
old.meta: FREE · lifeguard in season · organised sunbeds in summer · state-monitored, PAKOE contradicts

calas:Ormos Afroditis (Aphrodite Cove) r.group: In town: the pebble and the rock

old.name: Ormos Afroditis (Aphrodite Cove) rocks
old.teaser: Flat-rock swim under a seaman's cross, the port's most local
old.text: No beach at all, just flat rock on the Piraiki tip, a concrete cross and the blue-domed chapel of Agios Nikolaos, patron of sailors. Locals call it 'o Stavros', for the Monument of the Unknown Sailor raised on 7 December 1969; underfoot lie the fallen stones of the Cononian wall that once ran to Athens. Every Epiphany the priest throws a cross in and swimmers dive for it. The state lists no bathing water here and PAKOE flags it worst on the peninsula, yet locals swim it anyway, on a calm day after a dry spell, minding the sea urchins.
old.meta: FREE · no facilities · unshaded · unmonitored water · best at sunset

old.name: Batis Beach
old.teaser: The nearest real sand, shallow and free
old.text: The first real sand east of the port, shallow and warm and free, a palm-lined promenade at its back. State monitoring rates it suitable; PAKOE's 2025 round flagged it too, so cleaner than the Piraiki rocks but not island-clear. The coastal tram T7 drops you at Trocadero, the tram-away transition toward the Faliro seafront rather than central Athens.
old.meta: FREE · tram T7 (Trocadero/Batis stop) · lifeguard in season · organised + free stretches

old.name: Edem Beach
old.teaser: The clean-sand answer, about twenty minutes east
old.text: When the port's own water won't do, this is the clean-sand answer, a long shallow wade about twenty minutes out by the coastal tram T7, family-safe at the 'Edem' stop. Officially the cleanest easy swim near Piraeus, though PAKOE flagged a section here in 2025. For genuinely clear water, keep going down the Riviera into the Athens guide 's territory.
old.meta: FREE · tram T7 to 'Edem' (~15–20 min) · lifeguard in season · organised + free stretches
